newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air India to up Paris-India cargo capacity.
newsitem.headline: Air India to up Paris-India cargo capacity.

text.p: Air India said it will increase ex-cargo capacity on its Paris CDG-Delhi route significantly from next month.

"As part of Air India's policy to cut passenger and cargo capacity from Europe, our services from Paris have been progressively reduced from five Boeing 747 passenger flights and one DC-8 freighter service per week to two 747 flights a week currently," an Air India cargo official told Reuters.
"However, the indications are that the market cargo has begun to pick up again and 747-300 combis will replace the passenger aircraft on the route from June 1," he said.
"A a third, passenger, flight will be added on July 1," he added.
Cargo capacity will be shared with Air India's Frankfurt station, the official said.

"The new combi programme will more than double our ex-Paris capacity but we do not expect this to trigger off a downturn in rates, which have increased by between 20 and 40 percent over the past eight to nine months," he noted.
He said the rate situation, created largely as a result of under-capacity, was stable at present.
There were no plans to re-introduce the DC-8F service, which was withdrawn in July 1996, the official said.
Earlier on Monday, Air France said it had struck a deal with Air India which would open the way for a strategic alliance between the two airlines.
The alliance includes giving Air India discounts when using Air France's Boeing 747-200 freighters, an Air France statement said.
